Years ago, MacBooks featured a security lock slot, allowing users to secure their laptops to a table leg or similar object with a lock cable. These slots were particularly handy when you wanted to walk up to the counter at a coffee shop for another drink without carrying your laptop along.

Those slots have long disappeared, but you can now buy adapters to add lock-cable functionality to the MacBook Neo, MacBook Air, or MacBook Pro…

If you're a long-time MacBook user, you may still remember that built-in security slot on the side of the chassis. The slot worked with a T-shaped accessory: you insert the accessory into the slot, rotate it 90 degrees, and lock it in place. The most common design is a lock cable that can be threaded through a table leg at a coffee shop or library.

CompuLock has brought this idea back to life, launching an adapter that can be mounted to the corner or edge of a MacBook so a lock cable can be attached. The adapter uses a two-piece design, clamping onto the MacBook with screws.

In addition to the existing MacBook Air and MacBook Pro versions, the company has now added a MacBook Neo version.

It's worth stressing that locks of this kind have always been only a low-level security measure — their purpose is just to stop someone from snatching your MacBook in the few seconds you're distracted. I've used one in a smaller coffee shop where I could still see my table when I went to order another tea, and it gave me peace of mind; but if my MacBook were out of sight, I would never rely on a lock like this.

At US$70, the adapter isn't cheap, and you'll still need to buy a lock cable separately; but if you happen to have an old lock cable lying in a drawer, it might be worth digging it out and giving it a new lease of life.
